statement: Let L be a nonzero separable Hilbert space, let D ⊆ B(L) be a unital norm- separable C∗-algebra with Z(D) = CIL, and let P, Q ⊆ D be unital C∗-subalgebras containing IL. On H = L n≥1 L, define ED(P) = {(xn)n≥1 : xn ∈ D, xn → p ∈ P in norm}, (3) and define ED(Q) similarly. Then: 2 (i) These are unital norm-separable C∗-algebras with common identity, and dKK(ED(P), ED(Q)) = dKK(P, Q). (4) (ii) If a unitary conjugates ED(P) onto ED(Q), there are unitaries Un ∈ B(L) with UnDU∗ n = D such that, for every b ∈ Q, some pb ∈ P satisfies ∥b − UnpbU∗ n∥ −→ 0. (5) The same sequence (Un) works for every b. (iii) The two algebras have the same commutant, and hence the same von Neumann closure.
